terminal.name: run
terminal.description: Run a command in a shell and return its output. Commands are POSIX sh: printable ASCII, newlines and tabs; quote paths that hold spaces or special characters. Leave out `shell`, or give "new", to start a new shell (shell 1, shell 2, …); name a shell to run in it again once its last command has ended. Each command runs on its own in the workspace, with no terminal and no input: nothing carries over between commands, not the folder (`cd`) nor any variable, so join steps that need each other in one command (`cd src && make`). A program that asks a question gets no answer. Every command goes through this session's permissions first, and may wait for the owner's approval. The reply comes when the command ends, or after `wait` seconds with the command still running: it keeps running, so follow it with read from the reply's `next`, with a long wait. DO NOT poll read with short waits; do other work meanwhile. Prefer a dedicated tool over a shell command when there is one. The reply is one JSON object: `shell`; `status` (idle, running, waiting, ended or failed); `exit`; `waiting` ("secret" while a prompt waits for a password, passphrase or code, which only the owner types); `output`, the screen as it showed from where you last read; `next`, where to read on from; `more`, whether more output is ready past this page; `skipped`, when the start of what you asked to read is no longer kept; `note`, when the owner must act; `error`, why a shell failed; and `refused`, why nothing was done.

command.description: The command: POSIX sh, printable ASCII, newlines and tabs.

why.description: One line for the owner: what this finds out or does.

shell.description: The shell to run it in, by name ("shell 1"); leave it out, or give "new", for a new shell.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the command to end before replying: default 30, at most 120.

terminal.name: type
terminal.description: Type text into the command running in a shell. The shells here take no input, so type is refused: give a command its input in the command itself (a here-document, or a file). Replies as run does.

enter.description: Press Enter after it: default true.

why.description: One line for the owner: what this finds out or does.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the command to end before replying: default 30, at most 120.

terminal.name: read
terminal.description: Read a shell's output from `from` (an earlier reply's `next`; by default where you last read). While a command runs, it waits up to `wait` seconds for the command to end or to stop at a prompt for the owner: use a long wait, not polling with short ones. Replies as run does.

from.description: Where to read from: an earlier reply's `next`; by default where you last read.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the command to end before replying: default 30, at most 120.

terminal.name: interrupt
terminal.description: Interrupt the command you are running in a shell, as Ctrl-C does. Refused for a command the owner started, and while a prompt waits for the owner. Replies as run does.

terminal.name: close
terminal.description: End a shell, and any command still running in it. Its record stays; run starts a new shell. Replies as run does.
